title: How lungs exchange gases
intro: The lungs move oxygen from inhaled air into blood and remove carbon dioxide. Breathing depends on airways, tiny air sacs, circulation and breathing muscles together. Feeling breathless can have lung, heart, blood or other causes.

sections.heading: The branching airways
paragraphs: Air passes through the nose or mouth, windpipe and branching bronchi to smaller airways. Mucus and tiny moving hairs help clear particles. Airway narrowing or excessive mucus can limit airflow without the whole lung being visibly blocked.

sections.heading: Gas exchange
paragraphs: Thin-walled air sacs sit beside small blood vessels. Oxygen crosses into blood and carbon dioxide moves out. Effective exchange needs both air and blood flow; a normal-looking breathing movement does not guarantee enough oxygen reaches tissues.

sections.heading: The breathing pump
paragraphs: The diaphragm and chest muscles change chest volume to draw air in. Elastic recoil helps air leave at rest. Pain, muscle weakness or restricted movement can affect breathing even when air passages are open.

sections.heading: Control and testing
paragraphs: The nervous system adjusts breathing to the body’s needs. Lung-function tests, oxygen measurement and imaging answer different questions. A home oxygen reading cannot diagnose every cause of breathlessness or replace assessment of a worsening person.

sections.heading: Protecting function
paragraphs: Avoid smoke and harmful exposures, stay appropriately active and keep recommended vaccinations current. Persistent cough or reduced exercise tolerance needs review. Severe breathing difficulty, blue or grey lips, chest pain or coughing blood needs urgent medical help. Before a consultation, note when a symptom began, what makes it better or worse, and how it affects ordinary activities. Bring previous reports if available. Ask the professional to connect the explanation to your own findings rather than assuming that a general description establishes a diagnosis.
